LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:


<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is a straightforward `-bin` package that fetches a prebuilt Tauri-produced `.deb` from the project's own official GitHub releases page over HTTPS and installs its contents into `$pkgdir`. Every component is consistent with standard AUR packaging practices for binary packages:

- **Source URL**: `https://github.com/InstaZDLL/WaveFlow/releases/download/v${pkgver}/WaveFlow_${pkgver}_linux-x86_64.deb` — the project's own upstream release artifact, served over HTTPS with a provided `sha256sums`. No code is downloaded from unrelated or untrusted hosts.
- **No build-time fetching of mutable content**: The `prepare()` and `package()` functions only use `bsdtar` to unpack the already-fetched `.deb`; there is no `git pull`, `curl | bash`, `eval`, or base64 decoding.
- **`package()` behavior**: The loop iterating over `data.tar.zst`, `data.tar.xz`, `data.tar.gz` reflects the actual compression formats Tauri-bundler produces (gzip in 0.18.x, zstd in newer versions). This is the documented, expected structure of a Tauri `.deb`, and the extraction destination is `$pkgdir` only — no modification of unrelated system files.
- **Dependencies** (`webkit2gtk-4.1`, `gtk3`, `cairo`, `glib2`, `libsoup3`, `libayatana-appindicator`, `librsvg`, `alsa-lib`) are the normal runtime requirements for a Tauri app embedding a WebKitGTK browser.

The maintainer email domain (`8shield.net`) and the extensive `keywords` array are unusual but are mere packaging metadata, not executable code — not evidence of a supply-chain attack. There is no exfiltration, no backdoor, no reverse shell, and no injection of attacker-controlled code. The only hygiene note is that the `sha256sums` value must stay in sync with the released `.deb` (updpkgsums) if the pkgver is bumped; this is a routine maintenance concern, not malice.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>
Standard AUR binary package, fetches upstream deb, no malicious code.
</summary>
</security_assessment>
